drafted_from: tools/pointillist-film/tool-rows.json (tool:render-a-pointillist-target-animation), examples/encode_target_animation.rs, test/pointillist-film.test.mjs; the example was run here with cargo
start_here: Say to your AI: "Pack my two-cell film at 4 frames a second into one target-animation file, animation.pfat." It runs encode_target_animation on your computer and tells you where the file is.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads one animation request file and writes one packed animation file.
instructions: 1. Install rust (cargo) and clone the Workshop repository. The first run builds the program (about a minute; a few seconds once built).
2. Write animation.json: {config, script, frame_rate}, with config and script as for a single frame.

3. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:render-a-pointillist-target-animation"} and runs: cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path trillion-workshop/tools/pointillist-film/Cargo.toml --target-dir /tmp/pointillist-film-build --example encode_target_animation -- animation.json animation.pfat

4. Nothing prints on success: the answer is animation.pfat, which begins PFAT and holds the target pictures and the timeline with the frame rate, for a viewer that works the frames out itself. The same request always gives the same bytes.

worked_examples.title: A two-cell film packed at 4 frames a second
worked_examples.ask: Pack my two-cell film at 4 frames a second into animation.pfat.
worked_examples.given: From tools/pointillist-film/test/pointillist-film.test.mjs (the target animation test) and run here with cargo: animation.json holds config and script for a two-cell film (grid 2 columns by 1 row, gap 0.1; limits max 8 columns, 8 rows, 64 cells, 4 targets, 4096 frame bytes; style opacity 0 to 1, scale 0 to 4; target 0 is a red cell and a blue cell, target 1 is a green cell and a yellow cell; one segment from 0 s for 2 s that weights target 0 by the constant 1 and target 1 by the input time) and frame_rate 4. The AI runs: cargo run --release --quiet --manifest-path trillion-workshop/tools/pointillist-film/Cargo.toml --target-dir /tmp/pointillist-film-build --example encode_target_animation -- animation.json animation.pfat
worked_examples.hands_back: Nothing on standard output and exit 0; animation.pfat is 60 bytes and its first four bytes read PFAT (the two target pictures, the one segment and the frame rate 4 follow in the fixed layout).
